chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The cavalry horses of the warriors in this world will be their horses in Paradise, and the robes of the warriors are their swords.'

And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibrail (peace be upon him) informed me of a matter by which my eyes were delighted and my heart rejoiced. He said: O Muhammad, whoever from your community fights in the way of God, and a drop of rain from the sky falls upon him, or a headache afflicts him, God, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him martyrdom.'

key_terms.سبيل الله: The way of God; striving in God's cause
key_terms.شهادة: Martyrdom; the status of a martyr (shahid)
key_terms.عزّ وجلّ: Mighty and Majestic; an honorific for God

ai.seo_question: What rewards do warriors receive for fighting in the way of God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith contains two prophetic sayings on the merits of jihad. First, the Prophet affirms that the horses of warriors in this world will be their companions in Paradise, and their swords serve as their robes — imagery emphasizing that their earthly military service carries over to the next life. Second, the Prophet relays a divine message conveyed by Angel Jibrail: even the smallest hardship endured during jihad — a raindrop or headache — earns the rank of martyrdom. This reflects the early Islamic understanding of jihad as a meritorious spiritual act where any difficulty incurred elevates the believer's spiritual station.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, (it is) narrated, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The cavalry horses of the combatants in the world would be their horses in the Paradise, and that the robes of the combatants are their swords’.

And the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> informed me<sup>saww</sup> of a matter by which my<sup>saww</sup> eyes were delighted and my<sup>saww</sup> heart was happy with it. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>! The one from your<sup>saww</sup> community who fights in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so a drop from the sky were to hit him, or a headache, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Write the martyrdom for him’’.
en.sarwar: 3. Through the chains of his narrator Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated the following: “The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘The horses of the people serving in the army are their horses in paradise, and the gowns of the fighters for the cause of Allah are their swords.

The Holy Prophet has said, ‘ Jibril (Gabriel) has told me something which has made my eyes and heart delightful, “O Muhammad, whoever of your followers fights for the cause of Allah, thereafter even if a drop from the sky falls on him or he experiences a flu, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, lists him as a martyr.’”
